title: Sowing and Harvesting
simplified_paragraphs: 有一个人经过绿洲，看到一位老人正在播种，就走过去问："你好呀，大爷。这么热的天，你在这里做什么呢？”
"椰枣树？”那个人继续问，"大爷，你多大年纪了？”
"我不知道，60，70，还是80……我忘记了……但这并不重要。”
那个年轻人说："大爷，一棵椰枣树长成要五十多年，长成之后才能结出果实，所以最后您很可能无法收获果实，还是别干了吧。"
老人却说："我吃的椰枣是前人种下的，我今天播种，是为了让后人能吃到我种的椰枣。”
traditional_paragraphs: 有一個人經過綠洲，看到一位老人正在播種，就走過去問："你好呀，大爺。這麼熱的天，你在這裡做什麼呢？”
"椰棗樹？”那個人繼續問，"大爺，你多大年紀了？”
"我不知道，60，70，還是80……我忘記了……但這並不重要。”
那個年輕人說："大爺，一棵椰棗樹長成要五十多年，長成之後才能結出果實，所以最後您很可能無法收穫果實，還是別幹了吧。"
老人卻說："我吃的椰棗是前人種下的，我今天播種，是為了讓後人能吃到我種的椰棗。”
pinyin_paragraphs: yǒu yī gè rén jīng guò lǜ zhōu， kàn dào yī wèi lǎo rén zhèng zài bō zhǒng， jiù zǒu guò qù wèn：" nǐ hǎo ya， dà ye。 zhè me rè de tiān， nǐ zài zhè lǐ zuò shén me ne？”
" wǒ zài zhòng yē zǎo shù。” lǎo rén huí dá。
" yē zǎo shù？” nà gè rén jì xù wèn，" dà ye， nǐ duō dà nián jì le？”
" wǒ bù zhī dào，60，70， hái shi 80…… wǒ wàng jì le …… dàn zhè bìng bù zhòng yào。”

nà gè nián qīng rén shuō：" dà ye， yī kē yē zǎo shù zhǎng chéng yào wǔ shí duō nián， zhǎng chéng zhī hòu cái néng jiē chū guǒ shí， suǒ yǐ zuì hòu nín hěn kě néng wú fǎ shōu huò guǒ shí， hái shi bié gàn le ba。"
lǎo rén què shuō：" wǒ chī de yē zǎo shì qián rén zhòng xià de， wǒ jīn tiān bō zhǒng， shì wèi le ràng hòu rén néng chī dào wǒ zhòng de yē zǎo。”
english_paragraphs: A man passing through an oasis saw an old man planting seeds. He walked over and asked, “Hello, sir. What are you doing out here in this heat?”
“I’m planting date palms,” the old man replied.
“Date palms?” the man asked. “Sir, how old are you?”
“I don’t know—sixty, seventy, or maybe eighty. I’ve forgotten. But it doesn’t matter.”
The young man said, “Sir, a date palm takes more than fifty years to grow, and it can only bear fruit after that. You probably won’t live to harvest any dates, so why not stop?”
But the old man said, “The dates I eat come from trees planted by those who came before me. I’m planting these trees today so those who come after me can eat their dates.”
english_full:
A man passing through an oasis saw an old man planting seeds. He walked over and asked, “Hello, sir. What are you doing out here in this heat?”

“I’m planting date palms,” the old man replied.

“Date palms?” the man asked. “Sir, how old are you?”

“I don’t know—sixty, seventy, or maybe eighty. I’ve forgotten. But it doesn’t matter.”

The young man said, “Sir, a date palm takes more than fifty years to grow, and it can only bear fruit after that. You probably won’t live to harvest any dates, so why not stop?”

But the old man said, “The dates I eat come from trees planted by those who came before me. I’m planting these trees today so those who come after me can eat their dates.”
